verses.text: Saul agreed that Stephen should be killed. On that day a great attack began against the church in Jerusalem. All the believers except the apostles were scattered through the lands of Judea and Samaria.
Some godly men buried Stephen and cried loudly over him.
But Saul was trying to destroy the church. He went from house to house, dragged off men and women, and threw them into prison.
Those who had been scattered went everywhere, preaching the word.
Philip went down to a city in Samaria and told the people about the Christ.
When the crowds heard Philip and saw the signs he did, they all listened closely to what he said.
Evil spirits came out of many people, screaming loudly. And many who could not move or could not walk were healed.
So there was great joy in that city.
Now a man named Simon had been practising magic in that city for some time. He amazed the people of Samaria and claimed to be someone great.
Everyone, from the least to the greatest, listened to him and said, "This man is the power of God that is called Great."
They followed him because he had amazed them with his magic for a long time.
But Philip told them the good news about God's Kingdom and the name of Jesus Christ. They believed him, and both men and women were baptised.
Simon himself also believed and was baptised. He followed Philip everywhere, amazed by the great signs and miracles he saw.
When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that the people of Samaria had accepted God's word, they sent Peter and John to them.
When Peter and John arrived, they prayed for the new believers to receive the Holy Spirit.
The Holy Spirit had not yet come on any of them. They had only been baptised in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then Peter and John placed their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
When Simon saw that the Spirit was given when the apostles placed their hands on people, he offered them money.
He said, "Give me this power too, so that anyone I place my hands on will receive the Holy Spirit."
Peter answered, "May your money be destroyed with you, because you thought you could buy God's gift with money!
You have no part or share in this work, because your heart is not right with God.
Turn away from this evil and pray to the Lord. Perhaps he will forgive you for having such a thought in your heart.
I can see that you are full of bitter jealousy and are a prisoner of sin."
Then Simon answered, "Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said will happen to me."
After Peter and John had told what they knew and preached the word of the Lord, they went back to Jerusalem. On the way they preached the good news in many villages of Samaria.
Then an angel of the Lord said to Philip, "Get up and go south to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza." This is a desert road.
So he got up and went. On the way he met a man from Ethiopia, an important official in charge of all the money of Candace, queen of Ethiopia. He was a eunuch, and he had gone to Jerusalem to worship.
Now he was on his way home, sitting in his chariot and reading the book of the prophet Isaiah.
The Spirit told Philip, "Go to that chariot and stay near it."
So Philip ran up to the chariot and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet. Philip asked, "Do you understand what you are reading?"
The man said, "How can I, unless someone explains it to me?" So he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
This is the part of Scripture he was reading: "He was led like a sheep to be killed. Like a lamb is silent while its wool is cut, he did not open his mouth.
When he was put to shame, he was not treated fairly. Who can speak of his descendants? For his life was taken from the earth."
The official asked Philip, "Please tell me, who is the prophet talking about? Himself or someone else?"
Then Philip began with that same Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.
As they travelled along the road, they came to some water. The official said, "Look, here is water. What is stopping me from being baptised?"
He ordered the chariot to stop. Then both Philip and the official went down into the water, and Philip baptised him.
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord suddenly took Philip away. The official did not see him again, but he went on his way full of joy.
Philip appeared at Azotus. He travelled through all the towns, preaching the good news, until he came to Caesarea.
